title: Unit – 4 : Session – 7 | Symptomatic Relief vs Samadhan
sections: Q1. SYMPTOMATIC vs SAMADHAN: the current approach treats each problem — population, water scarcity, pollution — as an isolated symptom and deploys TECHNOLOGY for relief: more dams for water, contraception for population, scrubbers for pollution. Such relief is TEMPORARY and often SHIFTING: the dam silted or the aquifer drained deeper, the saved resources consumed by rising expectations, the pollution moved from air to ocean. SAMADHAN (all-encompassing solution) asks WHY the symptom arises: population grows from insecurity and lack of understanding (Kaam Unmad etc.); water scarcity grows from unlimited consumption and destruction of natural storage. TECHNOLOGY ALONE fails because the human assumption driving consumption and exploitation remains untouched — every technological gain is swallowed by expanded want. Only changing the human (education → conduct) addresses the root.

Q2. HUMAN-HUMAN problems (war, terrorism, depression, divorce, exploitation) and HUMAN-NATURE problems (climate change, water scarcity, soil degradation) share ONE ROOT: the human being's mistaken assumption 'physical facility is everything', expressing itself as SELFISHNESS (my comfort over others), GREED (unlimited accumulation) and APATHY (indifference to consequences) — in short, INHUMAN CONDUCT. The same Self that exploits a neighbour for gain exploits a river or forest for gain; the same lack of right understanding that breaks a family destroys an ecosystem. Hence there cannot be two separate solutions — 'social reform' here and 'green technology' there; the single root calls for a single remedy at the level of the human being.

Q3. WHY the solution must be HUMAN EDUCATION and not (only) technology: technology is a multiplier of INTENTION — in the hands of a Self without right understanding it multiplies exploitation (efficient weapons, efficient extraction, efficient advertising of wants); in the hands of a Self with right understanding it multiplies mutual fulfilment (cyclical production, renewable energy, restorative agriculture). Therefore the sequence is: (1) clarity of samadhan, (2) effort through HUMAN EDUCATION (right understanding), HUMAN CONDUCT (definite, harmonious living), HUMAN CONSTITUTION (frameworks that protect right conduct) and HUMAN ORDER (systems for the human goal); (3) analyse every problem in this light — seeing inhuman conduct as the cause and exploitation/domination as symptoms; (4) resolve the problem by ensuring conduct through education. Technology then serves as the instrument, never the driver.
